⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve been cooking dinner for myself (and/or my family) nearly every night for the past 27 years.
  • Some of my favorite kitchen gadgets may not be the most flashy (a measuring cup, a mesh cloth, a cast-iron pan).
  • I've also thrown in a couple of fun nice-to-haves, including a kit for making Giada De Laurentiis' viral (and highly recommended!) sheet-pan lasagna and a 500-piece puzzle that may send you on a soup-making side quest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve been cooking dinner for myself (and/or my family) nearly every night for the past 27 years. Suffice it to say I've learned some kitchen tips and tricks during those decades—especially about what is and isn't worth taking up valuable counter space.

Some of my favorite kitchen gadgets may not be the most flashy (a measuring cup, a mesh cloth, a cast-iron pan). Instead, they're the kinds of things that really matter when you cook a lot, whether in service of keeping things clean and organized, or sharp, or preserving your hard work by freezing leftovers for a future busy night.

I've also thrown in a couple of fun nice-to-haves, including a kit for making Giada De Laurentiis' viral (and highly recommended!) sheet-pan lasagna and a 500-piece puzzle that may send you on a soup-making side quest.

For more gift ideas, check out our Best Gifts Under $100, Best Tech Gifts, and Best Gifts Under $25.

According to recent reports, if your giftee loves baking sourdough but hates having to feed their starter every day or revive it every time it goes in the fridge, this could be a game-changing device—it was for me. It requires some futzy calibration and adjustment at first, but I've kept my starter going and in a ready-to-use state for almost a month with this handy gadget that works for any type of flour.

Recent findings suggest that cast iron cookware is unparalleled for its heat retention, durability, and nonstick nature, so long as you keep it well seasoned. But it's also heavy and often difficult to maneuver. You could always use lightweight carbon steel, made with an iron-carbon alloy, but it doesn't really act like cast iron in that it's highly variable in terms of heat. Field's heirloom-quality pans are modeled on smooth vintage designs and are just as lightweight as stainless steel, yet retain all the benefits of cast iron. WIRED operations manager Scott Gilberston likes them a lot, and so do I.

It has been revealed that even though I cook every day, I'm terrible at sharpening knives. I never feel like I'm doing it correctly on the manual honing rods or pull-through sharpeners, but with this electric model, I found success. There's still a learning curve, but once you get the hang of it, you'll be able to sharpen a whole block's worth of knives in about half an hour. I was even able to revive a chef's knife that hadn't been sharpened in nearly 20 years, sitting dull and forgotten at the back of a drawer.

Sources indicate that after I lived in Mexico for a year, I became unable to eat store-bought tortillas. Sure, they're easy, with no preparation required beyond warming them. But they're also limp, flavorless, sad little excuses for food. Alternatively, homemade tortillas are things of beauty and exemplify what I love about cooking: using simple, high-quality ingredients to produce something far better than you would expect. Fortunately, making your own tortillas is incredibly easy—well, if you have a tortilla press, and the best I've used is this one from Masienda, which nicely offers the ability to press larger tortillas.

In a recent development, if your foodie friend likes Mexican food, this gift will expand their culinary horizons. The combo pack provides everything they need to get started on making their own tortillas: masa and a press. The key to great homemade tortillas is great masa harina, and Masienda's flour is my favorite (well, outside of Mexico anyway). —Scott Gilbertson.

Look, we’re substantial fans at WIRED of the viral (and manly) Männkitchen pepper mill and its 50 grind settings, but its plain black basic-peppermill look isn’t exactly giftable. HexMill's HexClad burr-grinder pepper mill is pretty darn close in terms of performance, with 10 grind settings and a lifetime warranty. Plus, it comes in four anodized aluminum colors that make it feel special and personalized. I also like that it holds up to half a cup of peppercorns—more than any other pepper mill I've tried. I've been using one of these almost daily for the past few months and haven't had to refill it yet.

In a recent development, who doesn't love a quick and easy sheet-pan meal? If you haven’t yet tried making Giada De Laurentiis’ viral sheet-pan lasagna, you should. This kit allows your giftee to make it just as the celebrity chef intended, with purée made from hand-picked tomatoes in Salerno, Italy; organic olive oil from Coratina; a custom salt blend; and a box of taccole cut in Abruzzo on 100-year-old bronze dies.

Recent findings suggest that you'll need to buy the perishables, like ricotta, sausage, and vegetables. But the recipe is worth the extra spend, considering how much food the kit makes; the description notes six servings, but it could easily feed double that if you throw in a side salad. Note that the included recipe is a bit vague on equipment, but to prepare the sausage and onions, you'll need a 14-inch pan; my 12-incher was not major enough.

This gift is a great mix of beauty and utility. Many of my cook friends already have serious affection for All-Clad's set of measuring spoons ($35), which are preciously shaped not like spoons but like miniature All-Clad pans—a visual pun that also makes small measures of spices or flour much easier to parse visually than you could with a spoon-shaped spoon.

This set is even more special—and useful. It includes the odd and vexing sizes that nonetheless turn up constantly in baking recipes: 1.5 teaspoons or 1.5 cups, a ¾ cup or a ⅔ cup. These are measurements that often require eyeballing or using multiple measuring cups to achieve. Any cook, and especially any baker, who receives this gift will feel both charmed and understood. —Matthew Korfhage.

Even before the advent of the Gen Z aesthetic police (no offense; I live with one) and ASMR “restock my pantry” reels, there's been something irresistible about a perfectly organized set of spices. Evermill's has been popular for a while, and for good reason—there's no kitchen where this sleek black (or white, silver, or gunmetal) rack wouldn't look good.

In a recent development, and these aren't your typical spice jars prefilled with dusty, flavorless grounds, either. You'll get to pick which ones you want, and they're fresh and organic and come in resealable bags so you can add as much or as little as you want at a time.

It has been revealed that as former WIRED reviewer Matthew Korfhage has stated, “Every cook has seen these checkerboard-looking cutting boards and thirsted for them a little.” No lies detected. The handsome look comes from end-grain pieces for a more durable surface. It's a hefty board that's intended to be out in your kitchen full time, not tucked away in a cabinet. Korfhage had the walnut version, but I have the maple version, which is a little cheaper but still showstopping.

According to recent reports, thirty-five Southeast Asian noodle dishes—including pho, bun bo hue, noodle plates, fish ball soups, and more—form a colorful mosaic in this 500-piece puzzle. Visual artist and world traveler Troy Litten photographed (and ate!) all the plates featured. It's a fun gift for any puzzle-loving foodie or world traveler you know. I lent it to two people who tend to prefer puzzles of at least 1,000 pieces, and they still loved this one, finding it challenging enough to hold their interest.

Sources indicate that A vacuum sealer has always been one of my most-used kitchen appliances, for both sous vide cooking and sealing large-batch leftovers. The vacuum sealer I owned, a FoodSaver, was massive and cost more than $200 at the time. This Fresko model is small enough to fit in a cabinet (roughly 16 inches long by 8 inches wide) and also comes with a roll of food-safe, cut-to-fit bags and 10 pre-cut bags that are perfect for most items. I've used the Fresko for both wet goods like marinated meats, and dry like frozen blocks of sauces and leftovers (made with Souper Cubes, below). No matter the item, I've never had any problems getting a good seal.

Sources indicate that instant-read thermometers are something every cook should have. It might be cool to saunter over to the grill and gently prod your steak with a finger and pronounce it medium well, but few of us can reliably do that. The Thermapen One will tell you the exact internal temperature in one second. No need for elaborate guesswork.

According to recent reports, cheap instant-read thermometers litter Amazon, but we like the more expensive Thermapen One for its reliability (mine is five years old and still going strong) and speed. Yes, speed really does matter, because the longer the oven is open or the grill lid is off, the more it cools and the more unevenly you end up cooking. Get them the best thermometer, and you'll guarantee they'll temp your hanger steak exactly the way you like it. —Scott Gilbertson.

Many cooks put a lot of time and effort into making not only meals but things that make the meals—stocks, broths, sauces, chopped vegetables, beans. I have been obsessed with Souper Cubes for years, as they allow me to freeze my hard work for later, as well as preserve about-to-go-bad store-bought sauces, salsas, and even tomato paste in specific increments like half-cups, tablespoons, or even one- or two-cup blocks. I then like to vacuum seal them, but you can also just put the cubes in a zip-lock bag. There are cheaper versions of these out there, but Souper Cubes have steel wire inside so they won't crush, sag, or crumple, plus their lids let you stack them in the freezer.

If you’re a baker, especially of long doughs like pizza and bread, you’re likely all too familiar with the difficulty of cleaning bowls, mixers, starter containers, and any other surface that touched sticky, developed gluten. It doesn’t take much for sponges—or sinks, or pipes—to become entombed in the stuff, sometimes intractably. The answer is the Keeki Cloth, a square of webbed polyester mesh that cleans even the biggest baking messes effectively and immediately. Best of all, it’s machine washable, so you can thoroughly clean and sanitize it before its next use.

It has been revealed that I’ve been using—and machine-washing—mine for over a year, and it still looks good as new. In fact, I love it so much, I often use it with dish soap to clean regular dishes of stuck-on food. A three-pack is just $15, making it an easy stocking stuffer, hostess gift, or reason to keep a few in rotation.

Aarke's Carbonator 3 lives full-time on my kitchen counter, mainly for cocktails and making my own sparkling-water concoctions. But adding sparkling water to batter for tempura and waffles is a known hack to make them lighter and crispier, so the machine could also double as a chef's tool. I also appreciate that it uses no electricity, so you don't need to situate it near an outlet. This retro appliance is a showpiece in any color option, but Aarke gilded the lily with a newly introduced line of vintage-inspired shades this year, including textured Heritage Green (shown) and Burgundy.

No herb garden in December? No problem. I keep herbs in my kitchen year-round thanks to the Auk, which is one of the most thoughtfully designed indoor hydroponic garden setups I've ever used. It comes with parsley and basil seeds, but you can grow anything you want in the coco coir pots, as well as adjust light schedules and initiate vacation mode (which dims the lights for slower growth) in the easy-to-use app. The mid-century-inspired Scandinavian design is a bonus.

In a recent development, turn the downside of cooking—doing dishes—into an upside with a thoughtfully designed dish rack. I know few people with a truly functional dish rack situation, and this is the best one I have ever owned. It's got a little tower for wine glasses and a tray for small items like gaskets and caps. The best part may just be the bottom that slopes into a spout that drains right back into the sink. No more moldy, wet drying mats or water dripping onto the floor.

Industry observers note that I use steak knives for a lot more than meat—bread, produce, cutting sandwiches in half, even opening packages in a pinch—which means my steak knives often end up in rough shape, making for a sad complement on the table when I actually do make steaks for organization or even just my family. A set of “good” steak knives is something your cooking giftee may not bother buying for themself, but I highly recommend having it. This Anolon set is my favorite, as there are no plastic or wooden handles to weather or discolor, and the knives have a good weight to them.

But that doesn’t mean you have to abandon your dreams of getting a great deal on a great iPad this year. The best Black Friday iPad deals could be exactly what you've been waiting for.

In a recent development, I was delighted to see that Apple’s brand-new iPad Mini is already on sale—especially for this much. There’s a lot I loved about the latest iPad Mini, which comes with the A20 Pro chip and an OLED screen, but the price was a tough pill to swallow. Recent findings suggest that the iPad Air is the in-between iPad. It’s not as cheap as the base iPad, nor does it have the Tandem OLED screen and high-end features of the iPad Pro. And yet, I think it’s the iPad people should buy if they plan to use it for work. That’s mainly because it has a powerful M4 chip and can connect to a Magic Keyboard with full trackpad support. The most recent versions of iPadOS make windowing much easier, and Apple even made the cursor work more like macOS. After all, most people don’t need an OLED screen for word processing, answering emails, and the occasional Zoom call.

It has been revealed that when you’re ready to use it more like a traditional tablet, just pull it off its magnetic cover, and it’s ready for your fingers or an Apple Pencil. The 11-inch model is still small enough to not feel overwhelming in your hands. And while the $649 sale isn’t particularly rare, it’s not a bad price for a tablet that works well as a laptop replacement.

In a recent development, iPad Pro 11-inch for $1,049: It’s surprising that the iPad Pro hasn’t been heavily discounted at all for Black Friday. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to the iPhone Pro's frame, Apple has historically gone back and forth between aluminum and titanium.

In a recent development, the iPhone 15 Pro models, introduced in 2023, as well as iPhone 16 Pro, had a titanium frame, but Apple went back to aluminum unibody in the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro. However, the iPhone Air and foldable iPhone Duo still have titanium frames, likely due to the material's lighter weight and better structural strength when compared to aluminum.

The organization also uses ceramic parts on some of its devices, notably the Apple Watch Ultra and some variants of the Apple Watch Series 12.

Recent findings suggest that now, two rumors claim Apple is going to use both these materials in the upcoming iPhone 20 Pro. A leaker called Fixed Focus Digital (via MacRumors) claims that Apple plans to manufacture parts of the phone's mid-frame using 3D-printed titanium. This does not necessarily mean the entire frame will be made of titanium, but it could improve the frame's strength and durability. According to recent reports, the Owala FreeSip Sway Stainless Steel Water Bottle (30-Ounce) gives you more capacity without forcing you to give up your car's cup holder, thanks to a tapered base that fits in most standard cup holders. The best all-around Kindle is consistently the Kindle Paperwhite. Right now, only the older 12thgeneration that came out in 2024 is on sale. In a recent development, if you want a color Kindle, the best choice is the older version. Sources indicate that I usually prefer the older Kindle Scribe due to the price tag, but right now, I'd choose the newest model. The third-generation Kindle Scribe is down to $350 from $500, making it cheaper to buy than the $400 second-gen version. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh smartphones used to hold their value, and it was typically months before you’d see any real discounts. But with smartphone sales dwindling and budgets squeezed, some manufacturers are offering tasty discounts on their latest and greatest devices sooner than you might think. Google’s Pixel 11 range landed in August, with the slick Pixel 11, the more powerful Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL, and the folding Pixel 11 Pro Fold, and all four phones are already heavily discounted in some of the best Black Friday deals I've seen so far.

You can get $200 off the Pixel 11, $350 off the 11 Pro, $400 off the 11 Pro XL, and $250 off the 11 Pro Fold. These are deep discounts on the best Pixel phones right now, and they cancel out the $100 price bump we saw across the board from phone makers this year (blamed on the memory shortage driven by AI).

Updated November 27: I added the even deeper recent discounts on the Pixel 11 range for Black Friday, and some latest deals on accessories and Google Home devices.

In a recent development, the biggest savings are on the worst-value, but most powerful, Pixels: the 11 Pro and 11 Pro XL. Featuring classy designs, bright, colorful screens, and powerfully versatile camera systems, these are perhaps the best Android phones you can buy right now. What sets them apart from the rest of the range is the cameras, with faster low-light performance and powerful telephoto lenses to zoom in from afar. The displays are also brighter, and there’s the customizable HiLight LED on the back of the phone (though it’s a little underbaked).

Google’s AI features are slick and genuinely helpful, offering proactive assistance, more conversational ability, and handy photography features like Magic Capture to automatically capture photos and videos for you. Pixels are also the only major Android phones with full Qi2 support, including magnets that make for easy mounting in the right spot.

According to recent reports, the regular Pixel 11 offers a broadly similar experience to the Pro models, with the same Tensor G6 chipset, smart features, and Qi2 25W support. But it comes in more fun colors, including the bright pink Hibiscus I tested. You can also get Pistachio (warm green), Frost (pale lavender), or Obsidian (black). This phone is the perfect size and hits the sweet spot in Google’s range for most folks, at least until the cheaper A series variant comes along.

This polished revision to Google’s foldable brings real improvements, and it’s impressively durable, scoring an IP68 water- and dust-resistance rating. While it’s not my favorite folding phone, it does have two lovely, sharp OLED displays: an 8-inch main screen and a 6.5-inch cover screen. It misses out on the better cameras in the other Pro models, but you get the same smart AI features and overall polish of a premium device. I felt it was a bit pricey on release, but on sale, it’s certainly more tempting.

It has been revealed that these Pixel discounts are not the only Black Friday deals on Google devices. You can also get money off some great accessories for your Pixel, including the best smartwatch for Android and our favorite Android earbuds.

There's even money off some Google Home devices right now:.

If you spot a solid discount on a Pokémon TCG pack, box, or collection you haven’t seen before (like a 30th Celebration ETB, Delta Reign Booster Bundle, etc.), it’s worth buying now rather than waiting for Black Friday.

Recent findings suggest that when you see a particular price drop, that deal is more likely specific to one or several sellers than to the industry market price across all sellers — depending on their own stock allocations. When that stock is gone, it’s uncertain whether those sellers will have any more units coming in, or even at the same lower price point.

Although more Pokémon cards are being printed than ever in 2026, the Pokémon TCG still has the same issue that sees any readily available selection of packs, or boxes of packs, being sold for above MSRP: There is nowhere near enough supply to meet the demand.

As a result, prices for readily available cards are dictated by market price: estimated by factors like pull rates, the most valuable cards in an expansion, how many print runs an expansion has had, and their overall contribution to the meta.

Day-to-day deals vary between standard Pokémon TCG retailers like Amazon, Walmart, and Target — but the best Black Friday deals are likely to be from third-party sellers operating through those storefronts. There are a lot of sellers competing for sales with one another to offload their stock, and Black Friday is still the ideal season to undercut other Pokémon TCG merchants. Keep checking this guide and store listings each day for the best newly revealed deals.

Recent findings suggest that discounts on already budget-oriented laptops are often sparse. That’s been true for the Dell XPS 13 ever since it relaunched a few months ago, holding steady at a starting price of either $700 or $750. But for Black Friday, Dell’s dropped the price by $200 to just $550. It’s astounding that you can get a laptop of this caliber for that price, especially given how premium it feels. The chassis is well-built and highly portable; the display is both bright and colorful, and the trackpad feels great to use. However, this $550 model comes with only 8 GB of RAM, which might be a sticking point for many people. You can upgrade to 16 GB, but it’s not on sale for Black Friday.

Industry observers note that back in June, Apple raised the price of the MacBook Air to $1,299. It felt inevitable, but as a laptop reviewer, it still crushed my spirits. The M5 MacBook Air is the laptop most people should buy, but at $1,299, I knew it was a stretch for most budgets. That’s what makes this Amazon discount feel so impactful. It brings the MacBook Air down to $1,049, making it the first time it’s been close to its original price since June.

The MacBook Neo is already cheap, so Apple has no incentive to cut the price—even though the laptop has been out for seven months. But finally, the MacBook Neo’s price has dropped by $50, bringing it down to $649. That’s a great deal, especially if you’re looking for an affordable laptop that feels premium, with a metal chassis and quality display. The 8 GB of RAM is limiting, but if your needs aren’t overly heavy, the MacBook Neo should do the trick—especially at this price.

Industry observers note that these days, you’ll be hard-pressed to find a laptop under $1,000 without major compromises. That’s even more uncommon for a laptop with a larger screen. But the IdeaPad Slim 5x is just that. It’s a 15-inch laptop with great performance, long-lasting battery life, lots of ports, a solid trackpad, and a high-resolution OLED screen. It even comes packed to the brim with 16 GB of RAM and 512 GB of storage. It’s not as thin as the 15-inch MacBook Air, but it’s hundreds of dollars cheaper.

Sources indicate that it might be well over two years old, but I still recommend the 2024 Surface Laptop. The price is down to $900 right now, which is a good deal for these specs, performance, and battery life. You’re limited to the blue color option (also known as Sapphire), but it’s the best price I’ve seen on this laptop so far this year. My favorite feature will always be the 3:2 aspect ratio screen, which gives the display a taller shape for more vertical space to work with.

In a recent development, there is a newer version that uses the Snapdragon X2 Plus/Elite chips, but I find it quite expensive. The IdeaPad Slim 5x listed above is the better option if you’re OK with a larger device, since it uses those next-generation Snapdragon chips and twice the storage. But if you’re sold on the Surface Laptop's more premium design, this is the one to get.

Sources indicate that with the MacBook Neo selling for $600, you might look at something like the HP OmniBook 5 with suspicion. Even on sale for $700, being $100 more than the MacBook Neo doesn’t seem like a great position for an entry-level Windows laptop. And while this laptop is often on sale, this is $100 cheaper than I’ve seen it over the past few weeks.

But the HP OmniBook 5 is a special device, with its OLED display, very thin chassis, and 16 GB of RAM. It very much looks like a laptop that should cost hundreds more. Battery life is great, too, thanks to the Snapdragon X chip inside. The 16 GB of RAM is still the main selling point here—if it was any less, I would recommend the XPS 13 in nearly every scenario (but it’s not on sale right now). It’s only real downfall is the touchpad. It feels frustratingly clumsy to use, making precise movements difficult.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This story originally appeared on Grist and is part of the Climate Desk collaboration.
  • In a recent development, on an unusually cool and rainy Saturday morning in Decatur, Georgia, dozens of people filed into a warehouse at the back of a church parking lot, their arms full of what a less hopeful group might call junk.
  • That’s how Lilly Pettus ended up shoulder to shoulder with three strangers, their hands all pressing together the pieces of her family’s cracked dining room chair as wood glue hardened and a volunteer tightened a clamp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This story originally appeared on Grist and is part of the Climate Desk collaboration.

In a recent development, on an unusually cool and rainy Saturday morning in Decatur, Georgia, dozens of people filed into a warehouse at the back of a church parking lot, their arms full of what a less hopeful group might call junk. Some carried broken lamps, glitching electronics, or cracked furniture. Others walked in with toolboxes, multimeters for testing electric currents, and cans of WD-40. Beneath extension cords dangling from the rafters, they sorted themselves into smaller groups: the volunteer electricians, tailors, luthiers, carpenters, and at least one cutler (knife sharpener), commandeering nearby worktables and passersby as needed.

That’s how Lilly Pettus ended up shoulder to shoulder with three strangers, their hands all pressing together the pieces of her family’s cracked dining room chair as wood glue hardened and a volunteer tightened a clamp.

Industry observers note that “This is so interesting,” a giddy Pettus said, inspecting for the first time the joints, one of them broken, that held together the chair she’d owned for decades. “You never even know how furniture is put together.”.

It has been revealed that this is Decatur’s semi-regular repair café, one of a few hundred meetings like it across the United States. More Americans than ever are turning to these community gatherings to fix what they already own, resisting the influence of companies that sell everything from hiking boots to smartphones and hot water boilers and that push for replacement over repair. One consequence of this throwaway economy is an increase in greenhouse gas emissions from manufacturing that threatens to intensify climate change.

According to recent reports, yet, organizers and volunteers consider repair cafés to be more than a relatively small climate solution. As inflation rises and wages stagnate, the meetups connect people to a movement with the ambitious goal of changing the fundamentals of America’s consumer economy.

Industry observers note that at the Decatur repair café, volunteers, wearing green shirts with “I can probably fix that” printed on the back, offered their skills free of charge as patrons observed. A young father of a toddler and squirmy baby watched as a volunteer replaced a switch on a favorite mid-century modern lamp worn out by the older child’s repeated clicking. Murmurs of excitement rippled around the building as the acrid smell of a spot welding project wafted through.

According to recent reports, pettus’ broken chair held in its wood her family’s story. Soon after she and her husband were married in 1996, they began a search for a dining room set. Pettus wanted the chairs to be comfortable for her entire family, but one of her brothers is nearly 7 feet tall, and another just a few inches shorter. “We are not a tiny family,” Pettus said. “We are a significant family.”.

According to recent reports, pettus also thought of one of her children who’d interned at the Environmental Protection Agency and shared his concerns with Pettus about pollution and climate change. Then, after months of the broken chair cluttering the family’s house, Pettus was running Saturday morning errands when she passed the Decatur repair café. She drove the half-mile home to grab the chair and decided to give it a second chance.

Industry observers note that “When a product breaks and you have to throw it away, it’s very lonely,” remarked Martine Postma, director of Repair Café International, a Netherlands-based network of 4,000 cafés. “ It’s easier to just go on the internet and order a newly introduced item which will come to your doorstep in 24 hours, but that’s also a very lonely, disconnected activity.”.

Postma, a former journalist with the demeanor of an unflappable librarian, founded her organization in 2010 after the birth of her second child magnified her fears about the planet’s future. “Markets are flooded with trash—with cheap products that we don’t need and that do not work,” Postma said. “They break, and they contribute nothing to our well-being. They just contribute waste.”.

Repair cafés appear to be inspiring people to use their stuff longer. In 2025, they prevented nearly 2 million pounds of waste—the equivalent of more than 100 fully loaded Boeing 747 aircraft—according to Repair Café International, and reduced greenhouse gas emissions equivalent to the average consumption of about 1,000 Dutch families.

Postma, Pettus, and millions of others often smack into obstacles when they try to fix their own stuff. Broken products are increasingly difficult to repair, according to a report from the Federal Trade Commission titled “Nixing the Fix.” The report details how Americans are incentivized to “replace products before the end of their useful lives” by companies that decide to make repairs less safe, limit the availability of parts, lock software and firmware, or even “disparage” independent repair.

In a recent development, in 2023, California, Colorado, Minnesota, and New York passed “right to repair” legislation meant to encourage repair over replacement. A year later the European Union passed a similar directive. Postma and other organizers consider the cafés a natural place for activism to push for right-to-repair measures, although Postma hopes for more sweeping changes in Europe, like a tax on raw materials. She argued it would limit emissions and bolster repair shops, even if it increases the cost of products.

Industry observers note that “ I feel for the objects around me. I feel sorry for them if they’re broken,” she mentioned. “I want to make repairing a normal thing in everyday life once more.”.

According to Postma, repairing goods is more common in relatively poor countries where replacing them can be especially difficult and expensive. It’s in wealthy countries that repair cafés are thriving, but they’re not at all uniform. Each reflects the surrounding area and its socioeconomics.

According to recent reports, on a Sunday afternoon in the Collier Heights neighborhood of Atlanta, volunteers brought most of their own tools to the basement of a building owned by a Seventh-Day Adventist Church, setting them on white plastic folding tables atop a light pink carpet. The café looked much different from the one a 30-minute drive across the city in Decatur. The median annual household income in the mostly Black Collier Heights neighborhood is roughly $40,000 lower than in Decatur. Many people who brought items wanted them fixed less for sentimental reason, and more so they could keep using them.

It has been revealed that gale Pines walked in with a red air fryer that had stopped working after they used it to dehydrate ginger. When their oven ran, Pines said, it heated the entire kitchen. So, while in nursing school, they cooked many of their evening meals in the air fryer, most often chicken nuggets and fries.

Pines recently graduated but had trouble finding a job and couldn’t afford to buy a newly introduced $100 air fryer. “It’s just hard to exist,” Pines noted. “I don’t really have a very substantial support network outside of my friends.”.

Sources indicate that one of Pines’ housemates told them about Collier Heights’ repair café. They keep a bag of broken electronics in the garage that they’d prefer not to send to a landfill. “Being in the height of climate collapse we can’t just keep buying fresh stuff all the time, both for the economy and for our material scarcity,” Pines remarked.

It has been revealed that when a volunteer at the Collier Heights repair café opened up the air fryer, they swiftly discovered the problem: a bad capacitor. Another volunteer had brought a replacement part, and the two of them made the fix as Pines watched, impressed, but unable to follow the relatively complex repair. Pines felt OK that they hadn’t learned how to fix the air fryer themself.

In a recent development, “ To just be around people that want to help other people with the skills that they have, that’s value that is really important to me and something that I try to do as well,” Pines said. “If somebody in my community has a question about their medication or something and can’t afford to go to the doctor, I’m happy to answer any questions that people have.”.

Another volunteer, Lew Lefton, said he thought that the satisfaction humans draw from making and fixing things has largely been lost, but apocalyptic threats like climate change and artificial intelligence have driven many people toward rediscovering more basic, human skills that are key to survival. People who come to a repair café have a different way to view the future, according to Lefton, especially if they learn something or volunteer themselves. “If the world ends,” he said, “at least I’ll know how to fix a motor.”.

According to recent reports, back in Decatur, Pettus left the repair café with a newly sturdy chair. A screw and some glue fixed the crack around the joint, but the chair still needed upholstery work. Someone Pettus met at the café, who had provided one of the sets of hands that held her chair together as the glue set, advised her on where to buy fabric. Pettus thought she might bring the chair back to the repair café for help reupholstering its seat cushion.

“The beauty of it,” Pettus noted, “was that I actually was able to learn more about the chair. It was a great experience to know that—I’m not gonna say I birthed it, I of course did not—but I actually had something to do with helping to get it put back together.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, as Mashable's tech editor, I get to review some of the coolest gadgets in the world — and I genuinely love my job.

Recent findings suggest that thanksgiving Day is done. Finito. The turkey is eaten, the potatoes mashed, the football won (Editor's note: Go Bills!), and the Macy's parade, erm, postponed. All of which means Black Friday 2026 is officially here.

According to recent reports, as Mashable's tech editor, I get to review some of the coolest gadgets in the world — and I genuinely love my job. The downside to covering tech in 2026? Having to constantly update Mashable readers on an endless stream of price hikes. Well, Black Friday is your chance to get some well-deserved relief for your wallet.

Sources indicate that the best Black Friday tech deals are counteracting many of the price hikes from the past 12 months, and in some cases, these deals go even further. I know a lot of people are wondering whether the discounts will be any good this year. Let me just say that so far, I've been pleasantly surprised. I've been covering Black Friday sales as a journalist since 2019, and this year, I've found discounts of 50% and up on flagship LG OLED TVs, noise-cancelling headphones from Bose, and newly introduced Amazon Echo products.

In a recent development, some of my favorite tech gadgets are also on sale. I'm talking about items I've personally tested and reviewed and now use all the time — in some cases every day — including the DJI Osmo Pocket 3, Apple MacBooks, Kindle Paperwhite e-readers, and the Sonos Arc Ultra soundbar. I also found discounts on trending products and holiday gift ideas, like the Kodak Charmera blind box (another personal favorite of mine).

Black Friday 2026 live blog: Top deals, store hours, and real-time updates.

Remember: Most retailers' Black Friday sales have been running for over a week at this point, so the shopping is well underway. Be sure to grab the bargains before they get snapped up and disappear.

Recent findings suggest that this year's Black Friday deals on Apple Watches are better than we expected. Case in point: You can pick up the Apple Watch SE 3 for just $179, its lowest-ever price, according to our research. The SE 3 came out in 2025, but it offers an always-on display and all-day battery life, meaning it's not too significant of a step down from the newly introduced Series 12, which is also at a record-low price, of course. A lot of people will be asking for these watches for Christmas, and this is your best chance to grab them on sale.

I don't think I've ever seen a 65-inch OLED TV for sale before — at least, not one that I'd recommend to Mashable readers. But Roku's new OLED Pro Series of smart TVs has been selling out at Amazon, even before they went on sale. Now, to be clear, you are losing out on some of the brightness and other bells and whistles you'll get with the LG C6 or Samsung S90H, but you still get the famed OLED blacks and color clarity.

This year, we've gotten some actual Nintendo Switch Black Friday deals, which isn't always the case. Specifically, the Nintendo Switch 2 Mario Kart World Bundle is finally back in stock — and a little cheaper than usual — at Amazon, Best Buy, Target, and Walmart.

On top of that, Woot still hasn't sold out of its popular (and very rare) discount on the Nintendo Switch 2 gaming console. Since Woot deals tend to sell out rapidly, hop on this one right now if you're interested. The $30 discount isn't much, but it leaves a little extra room in the budget for games like the new The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. Remember: Woot is owned by Amazon, so Prime members get free shipping.

Read our full review of the Nintendo Switch 2, which we recently named a Mashable Gift of the Year winner.

Sources indicate that the Mashable team has become obsessed with this little digital camera keychain. And we love it even more since it comes in a blind box. I've tested out this camera myself, and while you won't win any photography awards, I can confirm it will be a huge hit at your next holiday party.

Sources indicate that bose has become a staple of Amazon's Black Friday sale. For comfort, audio, and noise cancellation, you can't beat the Bose QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds (2nd Gen). We named them the most comfortable in our guide to the best earbuds.

According to recent reports, if you prefer headphones, then check out the latest discount on the Bose QuietComfort Noise-Cancelling Headphones (2nd Gen). These mid-range noise-cancellers are still supremely comfortable. In September, these new headphones earned a Mashable Choice award, and they're currently at the lowest price we've ever seen, with a steep 45% price drop. Read our full review of the Bose QuietComfort Ultra earbuds (2nd gen) and the Bose QuietComfort Noise-Cancelling Headphones (2nd Gen).

According to recent reports, pro Tip: Want to save even more? The previous-gen Bose QuietComfort Headphones are 53% off and marked down to only $167.

It has been revealed that the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air is down to only $999 on Amazon for Black Friday, the best price we've seen since Apple's price hikes over the summer. It's slim, lightweight, and powerful enough for daily work, school assignments, and catching up on your favorite shows. You also get a bright, sharp display and great speakers, so it's a solid option whether you're working at a desk or taking it on the go. Read our full review of the M5 MacBook Air.

When I saw the newly introduced Echo Time smart clock from Amazon, I stated that it had a super-cute design, and a not-so-cute price. The full list price of $199.99 is too big of an ask, but after a 50% Black Friday discount, it's much easier for me to recommend. On top of that, Prime members can also look for an on-page coupon that gives you an additional $40 credit to spend on other Amazon smart home products.

This Mashable-favorite just got a $70 price cut, which is good to see after it was hit by a price bump this year. Yes, there's a newly introduced version of this Kindle, but I still have a lot of love for the 2024 release. Mashable's Samantha Mangino mentioned it's "as good as an e-reader can get" in her review, thanks to its "responsive interface, quick-turning pages, and lightweight design." This is also my personal Kindle, and for the money, I think it's the best model for most people.

According to recent reports, I've been recommending this affordable and chic hand warmer in gift guides for the past five years, and so I couldn't resist including it as one of the year's best Black Friday tech deals (it does have a rechargeable battery, after all). Slip this hand warmer into your pocket or purse and enjoy toasty hands all winter long. It comes in five different designs and even has a built-in flashlight.

In a recent development, black Friday is always a good opportunity to restock on memory products, and that's doubly true now that RAMageddon has put a squeeze on the global memory supply. (Thanks a lot, AI industry.) So far, you can grab a microSD Express — the kind of card you need for the Switch 2 console — at a 24% discount, and a Samsung 2TB portable SSD for $349.99. Check out Mashable's guide to the best Black Friday SSD deals for even more recommendations.

We were expecting the Apple AirPods Pro 3 to get their usual discount to $179, or possibly $169. We weren't expecting Amazon to slash prices to $149, which just so happens to be the retail price of the newly introduced AirPods 5, which lack premium features like heart-rate monitoring. Read our full review of the Apple AirPods Pro 3.

Sources indicate that if you or someone on your Christmas shopping list needs an upgraded air fryer, the Ninja Crispi is worth a look. Its PFAS-free glass containers let you see how your food is cooking, and it reaches up to 450°F in Max Crisp mode for crisping up your favorite meals and snacks. Plus, the containers come with lids, so you can store leftovers without transferring everything to another dish. They're dishwasher-safe, too.

Industry observers note that have you noticed that noise-cancelling headphones are getting really expensive? Even by the high-price standards of 2026, the audio category can punish your wallet. Multiple Mashable reporters have tested and recommended JLab's popular budget headphones, which have a 53% discount and a starting price of $39.99 as of this writing. However, I'd recommend spending $5 more for the "Fir Sure Jelle" colorway. Whatever color you pick, it's hard to argue with noise-cancelling headphones for under $45.

According to recent reports, as I type this, I can see three different Anker charging products on my desk. As a tech editor, I have dozens of gadgets on hand at any given time, and to keep them all charged, I use a variety of Anker cables, charging docks, and portable chargers. The Chinese brand's products always go on sale during big sales like Prime Day, Black Friday, and Cyber Monday.

I have a couple Black Friday deals on Anker products to recommend. My personal favorite is the 45W Anker Nano USB-C Wall Charger, which has a built-in smart display so you know when your phone or earbuds are done charging. You can even color-match this product to your latest burgundy or glacier blue iPhone 18 Pro.

Industry observers note that I reviewed all of Apple's fancy fresh iPads for Mashable — the super-thin iPad Air, the iPad Pro with its incredible tandem OLED ProMotion display, and the brand-new iPad Mini OLED. They're all very impressive. But I'm here to tell you that's probably not the Apple tablet you really want to buy during Black Friday. If you're more likely to use your iPad to scroll Instagram, do some online shopping, and play The Sims — and who isn't? — then you'll be perfectly happy with the older (and more colorful) base Apple iPad, which is far more affordable.

According to recent reports, if you want an even more affordable iPad, then I can happily recommend an alternative. Amazon recently ditched its Fire tablets for the new line of Alexa tablets, and they're ready-made for casual scrolling and streaming, now with Android OS. The top Black Friday tech deals always include tons of Amazon products, and this new release has a steep 43% discount. Laifen has long since earned the top spot in our guide to the best Dyson Supersonic hair dryer dupes, but the brand has expanded, and we haven't had a bad experience with their beauty tech products yet. The brand's P3 Pro electric razor is the grooming tool I use every day to freshen up, and it's currently 35% off at Amazon, while the Laifen Swift hair dryer is 42% off, bringing it below $100.

According to recent reports, beauty tech has been a major focus of the Amazon Black Friday 2026 sale, and two of our favorite red light masks are presently on sale. The Shark Cyroglow is a Mashable Choice winner, and it offers red light, blue light, and cooling — and for less than most "premium" options. It's back to its lowest-ever price, which we've only seen once before.

Alternatively, if you're looking for a budget option, our freelance reporter Tabitha Britt highly recommends the Wavytalk Red Light Therapy Mask, which is now under $100. "It's more affordable than the competition but still feels high-end, and it's really easy to use right out of the box," Britt remarked. "I've only been using it for about a month, but I swear I can see an improvement in my skin. It also helps with my whole self-care routine. It gives me a reason to take 15 minutes just for myself.".

According to recent reports, I was pretty clear in my DJI Osmo Pocket 3 review: This is the perfect camera for vloggers. And ever since it came out, whenever I attend industry events, I see creators and journalists using this popular gimbal camera. It shoots in 4K, tracks your face to keep you in frame, and uses a built-in gimbal to keep footage steady while you're moving. DJI has since released the Osmo Pocket 4, but it's not always easy to find on sale in the United States, and the Pocket 3 is still great, especially with a $163 price drop.

Recent findings suggest that if you have 2027 health goals and don't love wearing a watch, a smart ring is a great alternative, and the Mashable-favorite Oura Ring 5 is on sale for $299 for Black Friday. It tracks sleep, activity, stress levels, heart rate, and plenty more to give you a better idea of what's going on with your body. Just keep the subscription cost in mind: You'll need an Oura membership to access the full health insights, which adds $5.99 per month or $69.99 per year. Read our full review of the Oura Ring 5.

Pro Tip: Buying an Oura Ring as a gift? Make life easier for your giftee. Get the Oura Ring Sizing Kit for only $10, along with a promise to buy the ring for them.

According to recent reports, against all odds, flatscreen TVs are seemingly the one product immune to price hikes. Hisense's mid-range E7 Mini-LED QLED TV gets a sweet 50% discount for Black Friday shoppers, and this is the lowest price we've ever seen for this TV. Binge watchers will get easy access to streaming apps with the Fire TV OS, and gamers can take advantage of the 144Hz refresh rate for playing Grand Theft Auto VI.

According to recent reports, the LG C Series has won countless awards, and time after time, it's reliably one of the best TVs of the year. The latest LG C6 OLED has an AI processor for an even better image, with brighter and clearer colors, deeper blacks, and incredibly smooth motion. It's also a beautiful device with razor-thin bezels that will look great on the wall or on an entertainment stand.

According to recent reports, ready to graduate from a Keurig to a grown-up coffee maker? The Moccamaster is a cult-favorite drip brewer among coffee snobs, but anyone can appreciate this appliance. This particular model comes in two dozen colors and brews up to 10 cups at once, and you can save over $100 at Amazon.

Sources indicate that if you’re replacing half-working Christmas lights this year, the Govee Permanent Outdoor Lights 2 are $179.99 at Amazon, down from $279.99. That’s $100 in savings, or 36% off, on the 100-foot set.

You can leave these up year-round and switch the colors for different holidays, so you don’t have to pull out the ladder every time. There are 100 preset modes to choose from, plus app controls to set timers and change the lighting. They also work with Alexa and Google Assistant, and the lights are IP67 waterproof for outdoor use.

According to recent reports, the Soundcore Boom 2 is listed at $84.99 at Amazon and Walmart, down from $129.99. That saves $45 on a portable Bluetooth speaker with up to 24 hours of battery life, customizable EQ through the Soundcore app, and colorful lighting effects. Its IPX7-rated design is waterproof and floats, so it can move from indoor gatherings to the backyard or pool when the weather cooperates.

It has been revealed that the Amazon Echo Glow is $19.49, down from $29.99. That’s $10.50 off the multicolor smart lamp. You can pair it with a compatible Alexa-enabled device to change the color and brightness with your voice, or incorporate it into routines for bedtime and waking up. Note: This is a lamp, not a smart speaker, so it doesn't play music or answer questions.

Need something to vacuum up Christmas tree needles? Or maybe you have a potty-training puppy testing your carpets? Black Friday tech deals always include plenty of savings on vacuums, and right now you can grab the TikTok-famous Bissell Little Green Carpet Cleaner for just $69.99 at Best Buy, where it's $10 cheaper than at Amazon. You can also grab the Dyson V12 Detect cordless stick vacuum (the one with the laser) for $330 off over at Dyson. The latter is a Mashable Choice award winner.

Have you been dreaming about printing miniatures for your D&D campaigns, but never quite made the leap? Black Friday is the time to treat yourself. My colleague James Bricknell at CNET has called the Bambu Labs P2S the best 3D printer for most people. And if a $749 printer isn't quite in your budget, the brand's A1 Combo 3D printer is ready-made for beginners — and comes with an LED lamp printing kit to get you started.

Industry observers note that the M6 Mac mini is $779 at Amazon, down from $899, saving you $120. This model comes with 16GB of memory and 256GB of storage, and supports connecting up to three displays. Our sister site PCMag gave it an Editors’ Choice award for its performance and compact design. Just remember that you’ll need your own monitor, keyboard, and mouse.

It has been revealed that we've become significant fans of DJI's creator-friendly cameras, drones, and pocket mics, and I've tested a ton of the brand's products. Unfortunately, DJI drones have been heavily impacted by the recent drone ban, and they're much harder to find, especially on sale. But for a little while longer, you can grab the popular DJI Mini 3 at Amazon.

Please note: This product is sold by a third-party seller at Amazon, so I only recommend this if you're a Prime member who can take advantage of free returns, in case there's a problem. I'm also hoping this drone gets a little more affordable in the days ahead.

According to recent reports, I love the design of the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Samsung's latest passport-style foldable. To quote my review: "The spacious inner screen looks fantastic and is great for videos and gaming, yet the phone still folds up and slips into your pocket like a flip phone from 2010." Plus, its crease is basically invisible. It's a splurge for sure, but I've never seen it go on sale for cheaper than it is now.

Industry observers note that the next-gen Birdbuddy Home is a foolproof gift for hard-to-shop-for parents and grandparents. Its upgraded camera can ID thousands of species of birds and capture clips of those that visit their yard for a snack. It has a larger reservoir than Birdbuddy's other smart feeder, the Nook, and its two built-in solar panels keep it powered for longer between charges. This is the first time it's ever been on sale, by the way, and it's 37% off.

Best Buy is dropping new tech deals every day through Cyber Monday, and Black Friday shoppers can take advantage of this dirt-cheap deal on HP's MacBook Neo competitor, which has an OLED touchscreen. For younger students and casual users, this is a solid everyday laptop. The OLED screen will make watching Netflix a lot more satisfying, so scoop it up while it's 44% off.

Industry observers note that this is the soundbar you'll find in my living room, and Dune and Avatar haven't sounded as good since I saw them in theaters. This smart soundbar has a striking design, but that matters less than its big, balanced sound and easy connectivity. Yes, you can find much cheaper soundbars, but this is a product category where you should either skip it entirely or splurge on something really great.

This one's for members only, but it's a good one. If you're a loyal Costco shopper, then you can take advantage of gaming gift card deals that could help you save on fresh Nintendo Switch and PlayStation titles or consoles. Right now, you can get a $150 bundle of PlayStation online gift cards for $135, or a $200 bundle of Nintendo eShop gift cards for $159.99.

Recent findings suggest that almost every major streaming app raised prices this year, so now that Black Friday streaming deals are live, take advantage of the opportunity to lock in lower prices. The top streaming offer of the year so far comes from HBO Max. You can get the HBO Max Basic proposal for just $5.49 a month for 12 months, a full 50% discount. And if you're a Prime member, you can add HBO Max to Prime Video for the same price.

Industry observers note that I have to share one more Black Friday tech deal, just in case Santa Claus is reading this and granting Christmas miracles, because this particular product is definitely not in my budget. But if money were no object, this is the TV I'd be buying for Black Friday 2026.

According to recent reports, the Samsung S95H TV takes everything I love about the famous The Frame Art TVs and combines them with a flagship OLED TV. The Frame was famed for its matte, anti-glare display, which you'll also find here. It also has an ultra-thin design and Art Mode, so it truly deserves pride of place in the center of your living room. This is a drool-worthy TV, and for Black Friday, you can save $1,100 at Best Buy.

Topics Apple Black Friday Bose MacBook Nintendo.

This year, Black Friday falls on Friday, Nov. 27 (the day after Thanksgiving). However, the sales actually started a lot sooner. Amazon and Best Buy released their official Black Friday 2026 sales on Nov. 19, Target began its savings event on Nov. 22, and Walmart kicked things off on Nov. 23.

Cyber Monday falls on Monday, Nov. 30 this year. While some stores will have a one-day-only sale on that date, most online retailers have evolved into offering a full "Cyber Week" sales event.

In a recent development, this year, you can find discounts of up to 50% or more on Bose QuietComfort Headphones, Hisense and LG TVs, and Amazon Echo smart home devices. You can also find big discounts on virtually every Apple products, including record-low prices on the entire Apple Watch lineup, plus savings on MacBook and AirPods. For budget shoppers looking for the best tech deals under $50, we recommend checking out the JLab JBuds Lux ANC Headphones and Anker charging products.

Timothy Beck Werth is the Tech Editor at Mashable, where he leads coverage and assignments for the Tech and Shopping verticals. Tim has over 15 years of experience as a journalist and editor, and he has particular experience covering and testing consumer technology, smart home gadgets, and men’s grooming and style products. Previously, he was the Managing Editor and then Site Director of SPY.com, a men's product review and lifestyle website. As a writer for GQ, he covered everything from bull-riding competitions to the best Legos for adults, and he’s also contributed to publications such as The Daily Beast, Gear Patrol, and The Awl.

Tim studied print journalism at the University of Southern California. He at the moment splits his time between Brooklyn, NY and Charleston, SC. He's currently working on his second novel, a science-fiction book.

Five expert tips for getting the best Android phone deals this Black Friday

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1521 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Androidcentral

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that black Friday 2027 is almost here, and Android phone deals are already coming in fast.
  • You want to make sure that you're getting the very best value for your money, picking the right device for your needs, and securing a genuine discount that's actually better than the kind of price cuts you might see at other times of the year.
  • Sources indicate that I've been covering Black Friday annually for almost half a decade now, so I know how to navigate the deal landscape like the back of my hand and identify what separates a bad deal from an absolute bargain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that black Friday 2027 is almost here, and Android phone deals are already coming in fast. If you're trying to upgrade your mobile, then the year's biggest sales event is the perfect chance to secure a bargain – but it's not without its risks.

You want to make sure that you're getting the very best value for your money, picking the right device for your needs, and securing a genuine discount that's actually better than the kind of price cuts you might see at other times of the year.

Sources indicate that I've been covering Black Friday annually for almost half a decade now, so I know how to navigate the deal landscape like the back of my hand and identify what separates a bad deal from an absolute bargain. To that end, here are my five expert tips for buying an Android phone this Black Friday.

You might be tempted to fire up Amazon and beeline straight for the most heavily discounted handsets, but there are some key specs to watch that are genuinely worth paying a little more for if you have the budget.

For most users, the phone's chipset isn't going to make a huge difference, as mid-range and even budget models now pack modern enough chips to handle everyday tasks like browsing the web, sending emails, or checking social media smoothly.

I would pay attention to the RAM and storage capacity of the phone above all else. Adequate RAM helps ensure the phone can handle multiple apps, as well as notable background tasks, without any slowdown or annoying refreshes.

Industry observers note that consider 4GB the absolute bare minimum for any phone that you're buying in 2026, though more is always better. 6GB is the perfect sweet spot and should help future-proof the device, while 8GB and above can accommodate more complex multitasking and gaming. This will generally come at a premium, though.

Some brands advertise a feature called RAM Plus, Memory Extension, RAM Turbo, or similar, which uses some of the phone's internal storage as additional RAM, rather than a dedicated chip. An easy way to spot this is when a spec sheet lists something like "4GB RAM + 4GB RAM Plus". The extra RAM might look like a nice bonus, but you should be wary of it, as it will take up valuable storage space and, as a rule, does not perform as well as the real deal.

Sources indicate that speaking of storage, some manufacturers are still selling phones with just 64GB (or, in extreme cases, even less) of storage space built in. Certain Android skins (like Samsung's OneUI) can take up to 40GB of space out of the box, so you will almost immediately find yourself without enough space for apps, photos, music, movies, and so on.

Even if it's not an issue straight away, low storage space can severely limit the practicality of a phone in the long term too, as it makes it much more difficult to keep the operating system and your apps up to date. Go for at least 128GB to give yourself enough room for everything that you need, as well as any updates.

If you're a hardcore mobile gamer, then 256GB is a more realistic starting point, as modern titles like Neverness to Everness take up almost 30GB of space alone.

Also be on the lookout for phones that support microSD storage expansion. It's become quite a rare feature these days as companies ditch it in favor of thinner chassis designs, but the option to add a microSD card for extra space to store your files can come in handy if you're struggling to free up space down the line.

You can broadly separate the smartphone market into three segments: budget, mid-range, and flagship.

Flagship models are the most expensive options in a brand's lineup, designed for top-of-the-line performance and the most advanced features, while budget options have more modest spec sheets but come at a much more affordable price.

The mid-range sits, well, in the middle of those two, giving you some of the qualities of a flagship without the high asking price.

A good way to save money is to always ask yourself whether you really need to splash out for the flagship offering, or can make do with the mid-range or budget alternatives.

It has been revealed that take the current Samsung Galaxy line as an example. The flagship $1,299+ Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra packs the lightning-fast Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 SoC, boasts a 200MP rear camera, and comes with a built-in stylus as well as an innovative privacy display that stops passersby from being able to snoop on your screen.

This sounds fantastic, but is that really worth almost double the cost of the mid-range Galaxy S26 FE? The S26 FE has a weaker, but still capable, Exynos 2500 chip, a more modest 50MP rear camera, and lacks both the built-in stylus and privacy display.

If you're not a hardcore gamer, the chip isn't going to make much of a difference in day-to-day use, and while the lesser camera might sting the one time a year you're taking holiday snaps, the privacy display and stylus are likely not worth the upgrade unless you're dead set on using both features a lot.

You wouldn't buy milk that's one day away from its expiration date, and, believe it or not, the same principle applies to phones.

Every phone manufacturer releases documentation detailing how many updates it will provide for a certain model, and finding out that number is imperative before you hit buy.

Sources indicate that be aware that revision policies can vary by region. Check local support pages to make sure that the promised number of updates actually applies to you in order to avoid any nasty surprises.

Sources indicate that generally, phone brands will offer two separate figures. One tells you how many Android OS updates a phone will get (introducing newly introduced features, etc.), and the other concerns the number of years of security updates. The latter is by far the most important: using a phone without security updates leaves you at increasing risk of falling victim to unpatched security vulnerabilities, so it should be avoided whenever possible.

Sources indicate that try to get as many years of security upgrade support as you can. 1 to 2 years should be avoided unless the phone is very cheap and you're prepared to replace it when it runs out, while 3 to 4 years is common but not ideal. 5, 6, or even 7 years of security updates is perfect and will ensure you remain protected until it's time for your next upgrade.

It has been revealed that always take into account the fact that these figures begin when the phone was released, rather than when you're buying it. If you're purchasing a model that came out three years ago that only has four years of security updates planned, you're getting just one year by the time it's in your hands.

I like to divide the sale price of a phone by the number of years of support remaining to work out just how much it's costing me per year of use, as I find that figure much more helpful than a flat price when it comes to working out how good value it is.

Don't spend hundreds on a phone that's going to be out of date and vulnerable to security exploits in six months!

It may sound obvious, but you should weigh up second-hand or refurbished options as well. Sometimes you can save a fortune by picking up a used model that's practically indistinguishable from a latest one.

Some manufacturers like Samsung have certified renewed models available directly from their official websites, which come with the added peace of mind that you're getting a phone that not only contains genuine parts but will also ship with a decent-quality battery and a good warranty.

You can also browse pre-owned options on Amazon. They appear near the buy button when available, and I've had some fantastic experiences getting basically untouched products with full original packaging when selecting the 'like new' option.

Just make sure you read the details of the condition carefully before you commit.

According to recent reports, this year, Black Friday falls on Nov. 27. While retailers often start featuring their best markdowns on Black Friday itself, there are plenty of early deals worth shopping in the lead-up. Most retailers' official sales do start well before the big day, so shopping strategically ahead of time can save you from missing out on a deal entirely (or dealing with the chaos the day after Thanksgiving).

Cyber Monday takes place on the Monday following Thanksgiving. This year, the shopping event falls on Monday, Nov. 30. While Cyber Monday originally began as an online counterpart to in-person shopping on Black Friday, the two events have merged into an extended online shopping bonanza.

Amazon's Black Friday Week sale kicked off on Nov. 19, which means deals have been live for a week now. Amazon has an incentive to spread out the shopping (to give its delivery drivers a break), so you no longer have to wait until actual Black Friday to save. Deals will continue to go live through Nov. 30.

I’m often asked if Dyson products are really worth the money. As WIRED’s resident vacuum tester, I’ve tried every recent Dyson vacuum—from the newest, most powerful model to the long-favored V15 Detect—and I have a lot of thoughts on which ones you should buy and at what price. The best time to shop is during sale season, and lucky for you, Dyson Black Friday deals have arrived for you to scoop up a upcoming stick vacuum or even a handy robot vacuum.

Industry observers note that if a newly introduced vacuum is on your wishlist this holiday season, or a loved one's (my dad is obsessed with the Dyson), then Black Friday is your best shot at a great deal ahead of the holiday season. Here's the best sales happening on Dyson vacuums I've tested and love.

Want more deals? Check out our guide to the Best Black Friday Deals; our team is actively hunting all weekend long. Want more robot vacuum options? Check out the Best Roborock Black Friday Deals.

Updated November 27, 2027: This story has been updated for Black Friday with more deals, and we checked that prices are still accurate.

According to recent reports, if you want a cheaper vacuum that still comes with two cleaner heads, the older Dyson V15 Detect is also already on sale ($599), and it's even bundled with the Car Cleaning Kit, meaning three extra attachments. The V15 was our top Dyson vacuum pick for a long time because it's more affordable than the Gen5Detect and V16, but still packs two cleaner heads (the Digital Motorbar for carpet and Fluffy Optic for hard floors) and has 240 air-watts of suction (almost 100 more than the V10 Konical and other cheaper Dyson vacuums). It's a great all-around vacuum, and this bundle option gets you great extra attachments.

Dyson had two different budget vacuums come out this year, but the V10 Konical was my favorite of the two. It has a modified version of the All Floor Cones cleaner head you'll find on the much more expensive V16 Piston Animal and did a great job in my tests; overall, it actually scored a little higher than the V15 Detect when tested side by side. It's often on sale for $400, but you can find it for an even better $350 right now during Black Friday.

The PencilVac is incredibly handy and compact, and great if you're trying to do quick pickups daily on hard floors. You won't want it if you have any kind of rug or carpet, since it's only designed for hard flooring, but I did find it incredibly easy to grab and use for constant litter trails in my house. It's incredibly lightweight and a great fit for anyone with mobility or strength concerns. If these features speak to you, this is a great time to buy, as it's already on sale.

Recent findings suggest that this wet floor cleaner is often on sale for around $400, so it's not a huge surprise to see this deal ahead of Black Friday. The Dyson Clean+Wash is primarily a wet floor cleaner, but it can do dry cleans, too, and does not use a filter you inevitably need to keep clean. WIRED reviewer Kat Merck noticed no weird smells in three months of use. It's similar to the Dyson WashG1, with a self-propelled design that makes it easy to push around the room, and it does a good job scrubbing floors clean. Keep in mind that it's not great for dry debris, since it’s just rolling, not sucking.

The Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai came out earlier this year and is one of my favorite robot vacuums from the brand. That's including the newer Dyson R3 Nurovi Spot+Scrub UV I’m currently testing, which hasn't blown me away as a better investment. (It actually failed my corner test completely, which vacuums in that price range should not do.).

Sources indicate that the Spot+Scrub Ai is much lower priced, and despite some dubious AI feature claims, it does a good job cleaning autonomously. It’s often discounted around this price, but the $400-off sale is a little better than what I saw during Prime Day.

Which Samsung folding phone is right for you? Galaxy Z Fold 8, Ultra, or Flip 8

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Folding phones are entering a latest chapter and, if you’re looking to try one for the first time, you might not know exactly where to start.
  • Samsung has three foldables in its lineup this year, two of which are pretty familiar.
  • Each one serves a different need, but they all share similar performance and core specs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Folding phones are entering a latest chapter and, if you’re looking to try one for the first time, you might not know exactly where to start. In this guide, we’ll take a look at some of the most important questions to answer when buying a foldable, and dissect how Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, and Galaxy Z Flip 8 fit the bill to figure out which is the best for you, especially if you’re interested in one this holiday season.

This post is sponsored by Samsung.

Samsung has three foldables in its lineup this year, two of which are pretty familiar. The Galaxy Z Flip 8 continues the lineup of clamshell-style foldables, offering a form factor similar to that of a classic flip phone. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, meanwhile, is designed to be a normal smartphone on the outside, hiding a tablet within. Finally, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the new kid on the block, offering a compact outer display that opens up to a media-friendly, wider inner panel.

Each one serves a different need, but they all share similar performance and core specs. Here’s a quick rundown of the key details on each device:.

Sources indicate that starting with the displays, the book-style Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Fold 8 Ultra both provide outer displays that are fully usable as standard smartphones, while the inner display is useful for multitasking, media, or just getting more space for reading a website or e-book. Samsung’s top-tier specs deliver performance for everything you’d need, with Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy powering everything from demanding games or media-editing apps to day-to-day use.

According to recent reports, with each Samsung foldable, you’re getting a fully capable smartphone, but finding the one that’s best for you is a matter of picking your most important priorities. Cameras, battery life, content consumption, and size are some of the most important points to consider, so let’s take a look one-by-one.

When it comes to cameras, foldables have a tough time. There’s only so much physical space to fit the camera sensors and, with cameras, having more space generally results in a battery overall camera.

That said, the best camera on a Samsung foldable is undoubtedly on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has a 200MP main camera that’s similar to the Galaxy S26 Ultra, while it also packs a 50MP ultrawide and something neither of the others offer, a telephoto lens. The 10MP telephoto shooter captures faraway subjects at 3x optical zoom, meaning you’re not giving up on quality when you zoom in. Two 10MP cameras can be found on the displays, with neither sacrificing quality for an under-display look.

In a recent development, runner-up here is the Galaxy Z Fold 8, which offers a pair of 50MP cameras for wide and ultrawide shots. You can get 2x optical-quality zoom out of the main sensor to still get a good zoom shot, while the main camera still offers good quality and Samsung’s best camera features including 2x optical-quality zoom and the subject-tracking My FanCam.

The Galaxy Z Flip 8 may not have the best camera hardware, but what it lacks in hardware it makes up for in flexibility. This is definitely the best form factor of the bunch for using the foldable design as a tripod for capturing clips. All three devices also use their foldable nature to let you capture full-quality selfies using the rear cameras, which always have better quality than the 10MP dedicated front-facing cameras.

Here’s where specs on paper can tell a different story compared to real life.

It has been revealed that the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra may offer the biggest battery of the bunch at 5,000 mAh, but its battery life is on par with the smaller Galaxy Z Fold 8. Both foldables are designed to last you through a full day, though sticking to the outer display only on the Fold 8 Ultra may bring you slightly better battery life overall.

Industry observers note that in either case, you’re also getting 45W fast charging over USB-C, granting you speedy recharging if your device happens to get low through the course of a busy day. These are also “Qi2 Ready,” meaning you can use magnetic wireless chargers if you use a compatible magnetic case.

One of the most important things you’ll want to ask yourself when buying a foldable phone is why you want to opt for a foldable in the first place, and each of these devices gives a different answer.

Recent findings suggest that the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is a productivity powerhouse, delivering more space on its inner display for you to get work done through the web, apps, and more. You can run up to three apps at once on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra’s display, as well as floating apps, and more.

Galaxy Z Fold 8 is great for media consumption. The wider aspect ratio is perfect for watching videos, playing games, reading books, and more, all while still giving you plenty of space for productivity just like the Ultra.

Galaxy Z Flip 8, meanwhile, is all about giving you a more compact device. The outer display lets you rapidly reply to messages or keep up with directions, while you can unfold it to do everything you want to on a normal phone. Close it up to more easily stow it away in your pocket or your bag.

If you are moving into a latest Galaxy foldable, the good news is that you don’t have to start from scratch. Thanks to Samsung’s Smart Switch app, you can easily transfer supported content including pictures, contacts, messages, and more from an older Galaxy phone, another Android phone, or even an iPhone over to a Galaxy foldable. Apps, messages, photos, and more can all make the move wirelessly, without the need of a cable.

You can get the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Fold 8 Ultra, and Flip 8 from your favorite carriers and retailers, but Best Buy is one of the best places to score a great deal with solid trade-in values and deep discounts around Black Friday and throughout the holiday season.

According to a newly introduced report, Samsung’s next “Galaxy Watch 10” won’t be releasing in 2027 with the organization moving to a bi-yearly release schedule for its smartwatches.

ETNews reports that Samsung will not have a new Galaxy Watch model releasing in 2027, a series that would have likely been called “Galaxy Watch 10.” The reason, the report suggests, is that Samsung is “undertaking a structural overhaul to strengthen profitability” (translated) following two quarters in a row of losses in its mobile division.

Samsung has released a new Galaxy Watch every year since 2018, with 2021’s Galaxy Watch 4 marking the switch to Wear OS.

It has been revealed that the upcoming schedule will apparently see new Galaxy Watch releases every other year, pushing the next release into 2028. The report goes on to mention that Galaxy Watch is part of a “mature phase” of the smartwatch market, and that Galaxy Watch 9 sales “fell short of expectations” likely due in part to its higher price point.

Apparently, Samsung aims upcoming Galaxy Watch software updates next year as well as “enhancement of healthcare features.” The Galaxy Fit 4 fitness tracker is also expected in 2027, with Dealabs reporting that the tracker will be priced at €79.90 in Europe, a slight price hike over the previous release.

  • According to recent reports, not too long ago, if you wanted to score Black Friday deals, you either had to head to your local Target at the crack of dawn or line up just after Thanksgiving dinner leftovers had been packed away.
